# Curated board images (`examples/kept`)

Generated 2026-09-14T04:01:13.000Z from 1926 captures in the 570 games whose registry status is `done`.

- **149** images in the main coverage set (`examples/kept/<game>/`), from **80** distinct games: 107 forced by rule 1, 42 added by the greedy fill.
- **137** further images in the corner-case set (`examples/kept/corner-cases/<case>/<game>/`); another 75 corner-case examples were already in the main set and stayed there.
- **286** images kept in total, from **151** distinct games. **1640** stayed in `examples/games`, 21 of them because they are unclassified and carry no rare asset.
- **30** asset types are RARE (10 or fewer images available); every image containing one is kept.

## Selection rules

1. Every image containing a RARE asset type (present in <= 10 images) is kept, no exceptions - including images that also hold unclassified pieces.
2. The rest is a greedy weighted set cover up to at least 5 kept images per asset type. Game diversity comes first: an image from a game not yet represented for that asset type outranks another frame of a game that already contributes one, which is used only when no other game has the asset.
3. Unclassified images (reading `ok:false`, or a `knight (no close match)` / `metropolis ?` piece) without a rare asset stayed in `examples/games`, corner cases included.
4. At most 10 kept images per asset type is a preference only; rule 1 overrides it.
5. Corner cases: up to 3 images per (colour, variant, case), preferring games not yet used for that bucket and images not already in the main set. An image already in the main set is referenced by its main path, never moved twice.

`games` counts the distinct game folders behind the kept images of an asset type - when a newer image of the same asset arrives from a game not listed there, it is worth swapping in for extra diversity.

## Corner cases

Cases are interactions between a board piece and another board element. Each is detected from the stored reading plus the board geometry, never from transient UI overlays.

### `board-edge` - 145 images in `corner-cases/board-edge/`

**Rule:** A settlement, city, metropolis or knight standing on an outer-corner vertex of the lattice - a vertex that belongs to exactly one tile (18 of the 54), so the sprite is drawn half over the sea and the shore tile art instead of over land.

### `shore-road` - 35 images in `corner-cases/shore-road/`

**Rule:** A road on a shore edge - an edge that borders exactly one tile (30 of the 72), so the road runs along the coastline with sea and harbour art behind it.

### `metropolis-tower-overlap` - 90 images in `corner-cases/metropolis-tower-overlap/`

**Rule:** A piece whose drawn sprite rectangle overlaps another board piece's by more than 2% of a building sprite's area. Measured with the real draw geometry (buildings 154 px at spacing/416*1.2 anchored -0.065*spacing, knights 0.35*spacing, the metropolis tower offset 0.28*154*pieceScale to the right). In this dataset the only pairing that reaches the threshold is a metropolis tower covering the knight on the neighbouring vertex, so both the covered knight and the covering metropolis are flagged.
